From above, the tissue surrounding the esophagus was detached and the tumor was excised. The resulting defect in the adventitia and muscular layer was extensive. A direct anastomosis was considered to be difficult, such that subtotal esophagectomy and esophagogastrostomy in the right thorax were performed.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 55-year-old woman presented with palpitations and dysphagia due to a large middle mediastinal mass. Chest radiography revealed a 7-8 cm smooth mass between the trachea and vertebral bodies. CT confirmed a lobulated, homogeneous tumor (75×57×80 mm) compressing the esophagus. She underwent thoracotomy with excision of the 8 cm mass, which required subtotal esophagectomy and esophagogastrostomy due to extensive esophageal wall involvement. Histopathology demonstrated spindle-shaped cells with fasciculated architecture and nuclear palisading (Antoni A areas), and immunohistochemistry confirmed S100 protein positivity, establishing the diagnosis of schwannoma. Her postoperative course was uneventful with no recurrence, supporting the benign nature of the tumor.
